 }

-/*
- * The room's chat rail squishes the table on a phone, and it is ours to fix.
- *
- * `.wp-room-chrome` (watchparty's roster+chat aside) ships pinned to
- * `flex: 0 0 20rem` in its own stylesheet (`room-chrome.css`) with no
- * responsive rule of its own — verified: `.wp-room-chrome-frame` is a plain
- * row flexbox, and nothing in that file's handful of `@media` blocks touches
- * either class. Measured live at 375x800 (a stub-`whoami` build,
- * `#/match/…`): the aside held its full 320px and
- * `.wp-room-chrome-frame__content` — our own screen — was squeezed to a
- * 55px sliver with no border of its own, which reads exactly as "squished,
- * no boundaries". `NARROW_BREAKPOINT` (768, `@wolffm/themes` platform
- * module) is the fleet's one narrow threshold; the literal below is that
- * value minus one, matching `NARROW_QUERY`, spelled out because a CSS media
- * query cannot import a JS constant.
- *
- * These are unlayered rules reaching into a `@layer`-wrapped stylesheet: per
- * the cascade-layers spec an unlayered author rule always beats a layered
- * one regardless of selector specificity, so this needs no `!important`.
- */
-@media (max-width: 767px) {
-  .cardtable-chrome .wp-room-chrome-frame {
-    flex-direction: column;
-  }
-
-  .cardtable-chrome .wp-room-chrome {
-    flex: 0 0 auto;
-    max-height: 45vh;
-    border-top: 1px solid var(--color-border);
-    border-left: none;
-  }
-}
